# services-dossier.md

**Research cut-off:** 11 November 2026. **Repository version:** `a131ad440ba5545edb0d26c5f8a7329560be6b5a`, committed 11 November 2026, 02:42:15 UTC. The complete README and its delegated canonical register, `data/services.md`, were read. This document preserves all 130 registered IDs, English titles and slugs. [W01; W02]

## Section 0 — Executive Summary

Tunisia has a graduate-employment problem, but the expression “130,000 unemployed experts” combines a programme design with a particular administrative population. INS estimates graduate unemployment at **26.6% of the graduate labour force in Q2 2026**, including **35.6% among women and 14.2% among men**. These survey estimates are not the stock of graduates registered at employment offices. [R01]

The reported Ministry/ANETI freeze of 20 February 2026 could not be independently authenticated against an admissible primary document. Its field, diploma and age breakdowns are therefore reported as **unverified claims**, not substituted for national statistics. The available age bands do not establish continuous unemployment since graduation. This limitation matters: W5D's equal allocation of capacity is not a measured distribution of either graduate specialities or paying customers. [G01; W01]

The structural diagnosis is nevertheless substantial. Private employment has favoured lower-value activities, firms report skills constraints, regional mobility is restricted, and secure public employment remains attractive. A historical comparison yields approximately six university graduates per net additional high-end job, using partly different reference periods—not a current vacancies ratio. Migration removes some scarce capabilities while other graduates remain unemployed. [R02–R09]

W5D proposes an organisational response: five macro works, 26 registered services in each, and capacity for 1,000 experts per service. The README specifies eight account roles, scoped authority, team caps, a weekly work engine, split SQLite databases and rollup-first dashboards. None of this verifies that the target workforce is employed today. [W01; W02]

The financial constraint is immediate. Under the README's 30-day convention, one recurring part yields 300 TND monthly against a 600 TND salary. W5D must choose between two parts, one part plus a 300 TND co-funder, or a revised 300 TND salary offer subject to legal review. Management costs, employer contributions, equipment and reserves remain additional. The dossier does not choose for the owner. [W01]

Operational detail below is explicitly a **proposed commissioning design**. Dyon competency profiles, a mandatory activation gate, numerical RAG thresholds and 5% sampling are not established README rules. All production targets require pilots and customer acceptance. Finally, universal incoming and outgoing service dependencies cannot coexist with a finite acyclic service-only graph. The document consequently certifies only a clearly time-indexed delivery graph, not the collapsed relationship graph. These qualifications are conditions of credibility, not footnotes to an employment guarantee.

## Section 1 — Why 130,000 Tunisian experts are unemployed (evidence)

### 1.1 Populations, dates and admissibility

“Registered demand” is labour **supply**: a request for employment recorded administratively. It is not a purchase order for a service. Survey unemployment concerns people without employment who meet the survey's availability and search criteria. NEET concerns people outside employment, education and training, including inactive non-searchers. A diploma, a professional registration and an assessed occupational competence are different attributes. No number below silently moves between these populations. [R01; R10]

The following baseline draws on nine separately dated Tunisia-specific works. They are not nine statistically independent experiments: OECD's historical jobs comparison reuses World Bank evidence, and ETF reproduces INS indicators. They provide complementary findings, not nine independent confirmations of the Ministry register. [R01–R09]

| Source | Publication / reference period | Population and status | Finding and permissible inference |
|---|---|---|---|
| INS [R01] | 15 August 2026 / Q2 2026 | National labour-force survey estimates | 622,400 unemployed; 14.9% unemployment overall; graduate rate 26.6%. These are not ANETI registered job seekers. |
| OECD [R02] | 4 April 2022 / principally pre-pandemic and 2019 observations | Labour-market and firm evidence, historical synthesis | Job creation concentrated in low-productivity activities; university/VET curricula and employer requirements poorly connected. This does not identify a defect in every graduate. |
| OECD [R03] | June 2024 / firm-survey comparisons including 2013 and Figure 3.18 labelled “2020 or most recent year available” | Covered formal private firms; survey-based shares | Nearly 40% identify inadequately skilled labour as a major constraint; reported foreign/domestic shares approximately 44%/34%. These are employer perceptions, not tested graduate incompetence. The report's 2024 citation is not a 2024 census. |
| World Bank [R04] | 2022 / employment 2011–2017; academic years 2012/13–2017/18 | Estimated annual graduate flow versus net occupational employment growth | 64,540 graduates per year against 10,675 net additional high-end jobs per year; computed ratio ≈6.05:1. Periods differ and net growth is not gross hiring. |
| World Bank [R05] | Cover 06/01/2026; catalogue indicates 1 June 2026 / platform data through 2025 | LinkedIn and Lightcast users and online postings; coverage-biased | Demand extends beyond ICT into digitally enabled logistics, manufacturing, finance, energy and agriculture. Postings are neither filled posts nor a representative national vacancy census. |
| ETF [R06] | September 2021 / mainly 2019–2021 | Institutional migration/skills review | Skills migration and fragmented institutional responsibilities weaken retention and coordination; mobility programmes do not automatically create employment in Tunisia. |
| Kotrane [R07] | Journal issue 3, 2024 / policy and legal position discussed in 2024 | Peer-reviewed legal analysis, not an impact evaluation | Training and insertion mechanisms coexist with formal-job scarcity and unequal access; eligibility and protection require legal examination. |
| World Bank CCDR [R08] | November 2023 / water observations including 2021; future scenarios separately labelled | Historical system indicators and conditional climate modelling | SONEDE distribution losses reported at 34% in 2021, versus 25% in 2010; water, coastal protection and energy transition require coordinated technical work, not necessarily already financed vacancies. |
| INS/ONM HIMS [R09] | 7 December 2021 / survey July 2020–March 2021; departures 2015–2020 | Retrospective household-survey estimates under defined migrant coverage | Approximately 39,000 engineers and 3,300 medical doctors reportedly left during 2015–2020; these are estimates, not Order-register exit counts or a two-year flow. |

### 1.2 The frozen Ministry register: confirmation limits

An admissible copy of the written Ministry response, its tables, definitions, revision history and parliamentary identifier was not located. Dated secondary accounts corroborate the existence of the claim, but the user's admissibility rule excludes those accounts as proof. The values below remain **not independently confirmed against an admissible primary source**. They are not converted into per-service headcounts. [G01]

| Requested administrative statistic | Reported value, not verified here | Interpretation limit |
|---|---|---|
| Registered higher-education job seekers, freeze 20 February 2026 | More than 130,000; one secondary account gives 130,612 | No authenticated extract establishing active registration, deduplication or unemployment status. |
| Field of study | Sciences/technology 39.4%; management/law 30.3%; letters/humanities 24.1% | Sum 93.8%; unexplained remainder must not be redistributed. Not a five-macro staffing allocation. |
| Diploma | Licence/maîtrise 73%; technician diplomas 12%; third cycle 10% | Broad categories sum to 95%; overlaps and residual categories unresolved. |
| Specific diplomas | 3,891 engineers; 110 holders of a doctorat | Doctorat holders are not necessarily medical doctors. Membership of the Order is not established. |
| Age bands | 30–40: 44.9%; 40–50: 42% | Together 86.9% in the reported 30–50 bands, not proof that exactly 87% of all registrants are over 30; upper-band boundaries and 50+ remain unresolved. |
| Graduation year | More than 90% reportedly graduated in 2021 or earlier; approximately 117,000; 2025 graduates 3.5% | Graduation date is not duration of uninterrupted unemployment. Counts and percentages may use rounded or different totals. |

A programme intended to reach this reported older cohort should prioritise re-entry, recognition of prior learning, accessible local placements, caring responsibilities and paid work—not treat every applicant as a recent school leaver. However, the age and duration profile must be authenticated before quotas or eligibility algorithms are adopted. [R02; R06; G01]

### 1.3 Engineers: three denominators that cannot be reconciled by division

| Population | Requested figure and evidence status | What remains unavailable |
|---|---|---|
| Engineers registered at employment offices | Claimed 3,891, frozen 20 February 2026; unverified primary extract [G01] | Active registration definition, speciality, overlap with Order, current employment. |
| Engineers inscribed at the Ordre des Ingénieurs Tunisiens | **~23% unemployed — estimate, method not public**; primary statistical release not authenticated [G02] | Survey date, response rate, denominator, treatment of emigrants and inactive registrants. |
| Agricultural engineers allegedly within the Order population | **~15,000 of ~20,000 unemployed or precariously employed**; primary membership coverage and method unverified [G03] | Whether denominator is Order membership, all graduates, economically active residents, or another population. |

The last claim would imply roughly 75% in a **combined unemployment/precarity category**, if its numerator and denominator were valid. It would not establish a 75% unemployment rate. The ~23% estimate and the agricultural claim are separate assertions; neither is multiplied by the ANETI stock. A valid reconciliation needs linked, consented, dated records and explicit residency and labour-force status. [G01–G03]

### 1.4 Brain drain without false precision

The requests “95% of IT engineers abroad”, “40,000 engineers emigrated in two years” and “at least 20 per day” were not confirmed against admissible data with a defined population and interval. They are listed as unverified leads, not quantitative premises. The retrospective HIMS estimate of **~39,000 engineers and ~3,300 medical doctors during 2015–2020** is a different, admissible finding. Dividing a retrospective survey estimate into a daily headline does not create a measured daily departure series. [R09; G04]

IT skills can access international markets and remote recruitment; health qualifications and experience are also internationally recruited, subject to recognition rules. Language, career opportunities, working conditions and pay influence these choices. Better-qualified workers leaving can coexist with unemployment among other graduates: occupation labels conceal experience, competency and geographic differences. Neither the availability of unemployed graduates nor a Dyon credential alone establishes retention capacity. [R02; R05; R06; R09]

### 1.5 Structural mechanisms

**Mismatch is multidimensional.** Firms may need practical digital, language, teamwork and domain-specific skills while graduates hold qualifications that signal different competencies. The nearly 40% employer-constraint finding is consistent with this problem, but also with unattractive conditions, poor recruitment practices and restricted mobility. It is not a reason to blame unemployed people collectively. [R02; R03]

**Overqualification reflects demand composition.** Figure O.15's approximately six-to-one comparison concerns historical graduate output versus net high-end job creation, not six applicants per vacancy today. Using its 53,056 average annual total employment increase gives 64,540/53,056 ≈1.22 graduates per net additional job. OECD's “25% more” summary is rounded and not reproduced exactly by that figure; the dossier uses the transparent figure-based calculation. Training alone cannot change the occupational structure of all new jobs. [R03; R04]

**Public-sector preference is partly rational.** Security, leave, predictable careers and social protection matter. World Bank reports approximately 75.9% of unemployed tertiary-educated people aged 25–34 living as children in their parents' households in 2015. This is historical evidence of family dependence, not proof that they voluntarily rejected decent private offers. Fiscal constraints on recruitment cannot be treated as an indefinitely verified blanket hiring freeze in 2026. [R02; R04; R06]

**Regional mismatch is not simply rural unemployment.** Economic activity and skilled hiring concentrate in coastal hubs. Transport, housing, household dependence and constraints on women's mobility restrict access. INS Q2 2026 urban/rural unemployment rates, 14.8%/15.0%, use labour-force denominators and cannot supply rural/urban NEET rates. No current Tunisia-specific rural-to-urban NEET ratio was authenticated. The ILO's general rural NEET pattern is methodological context, not a Tunisian estimate. [R01; R02; R03; R10]

**Gender is central.** INS estimates graduate unemployment at 35.6% among women versus 14.2% among men in Q2 2026, a computed 21.4 percentage-point gap. Local accessible work, safe travel, predictable schedules and care support are therefore programme-design hypotheses worth testing, not optional publicity measures. [R01; R02]

**Informality changes the available offer.** OECD's 2022 review reports 45% overall informality for 2019, with especially high rates in agriculture, construction and retail under the cited definition. OECD 2024 also discusses almost 40% of **non-agricultural** employment: different denominators, not contradictory measurements of the same population. A nominal placement without enforceable pay, safety and social protection does not solve graduate exclusion. [R02; R03; R07]

### 1.6 Absorptive capacity: need, opportunity and funded work

| Sector or capability | Evidence-based signal | What cannot be claimed |
|---|---|---|
| Software, cloud, cybersecurity, data and hybrid digital roles | Recent online-demand evidence, with urban/formal/platform coverage limitations [R05] | Neither a national shortage count nor 1,000 vacancies in every advanced speciality. |
| Business, scientific and technical services | Higher-skill employment potential and FDI presence [R02; R03] | Foreign-firm presence is not an unlimited local hiring commitment. |
| Agriculture and food quality systems | Traceability, testing, certification and coordination constrain upgrading [R02]; water constraints are documented [R08] | Seasonal farm labour shortages do not prove demand for all unemployed agricultural engineers. |
| Water networks, energy efficiency, renewables and climate resilience | Documented losses, scarcity, adaptation and investment needs [R08] | A social need or modelled future job scenario is not a procured, funded post today. |
| Textiles, construction and tourism | Historical employer recruitment difficulties [R02; R03] | Unfilled low-paid or geographically inaccessible jobs are not automatically suitable graduate employment. |
| Humanities, social sciences and public-service-oriented qualifications | Historically weak private absorption and public-employment orientation [R02; R04] | No authenticated 2026 field-by-field vacancy/supply ratio; no basis for declaring every individual oversupplied. |

The only explicitly calculated supply/absorption ratio retained is the historical **≈6.05:1**, with its non-identical periods and net-flow limitations. Current sector-specific ratios remain **not established**. Equal service caps are an organisational choice requiring phased validation, not an empirical finding about these ratios. [R04; W01]

## Section 2 — Why existing interventions have not absorbed them

Absence of full absorption does not demonstrate that an intervention had no effect. A causal claim requires a comparison group, implementation data and a defined outcome. The table identifies structural reach limits; it does not invent evaluations. Historical rules are not represented as confirmed current eligibility. [R02; R04; R07]

| Response | What it does | Dated scale / evidence | Structural limit for an applicant aged 30+ with a long employment gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANETI matching and insertion support | Registers applicants, mediates vacancies and administers insertion mechanisms | National institution documented in ETF September 2021; current beneficiary total not authenticated [R06; G01] | Better matching cannot create every missing high-skill job; transport, care, employer selection and stale skill signals remain. |
| CIVP and KARAMA | Subsidise insertion and support employer-based skill acquisition | Kotrane's 2024 account describes CIVP's then-applicable duration and KARAMA's 600 TND salary with subsidy up to 400 TND; national placement totals not established [R07] | Require a host employer and compatible eligibility; an older first-time seeker may qualify. Do not assert an automatic age exclusion. Current 2026 rules need verification. |
| Public recruitment and constrained hiring | Can absorb qualified staff into authorised services | OECD April 2022 fiscal-space diagnosis; ETF September 2021 describes recruitment constraints/freeze in its historical context; no verified blanket 2026 freeze or current absorption count [R02; R06] | Recruitment depends on funded statutory establishments and selection; it cannot be assumed to cover all older registered graduates. |
| Vocational education and continuing training | Develops occupational competence and retrains workers | Peer-reviewed 2024 inventory reports approximately 136 ATFP institutions and 300 specialities; facilities are not successful placements [R07] | Training requires an actual destination job and accessible participation; repeated certificates alone do not fund work or resolve household obligations. |
| Entrepreneurship and the Startup Act | Eases entry and supports innovative firms | Act introduced in 2018, analysed by OECD in April 2022; no current supported-founder/employment total verified [R02] | Customers, working capital, regulation and risk tolerance constrain entry. Not every unemployed professional should become an entrepreneur or pledge household assets. |
| Diaspora cooperation and ATCT | Mobilises expertise, investment and international placements | ETF September 2021: historical ATCT placement estimate 2,000–3,000 highly qualified people annually; Perspectives commitment EUR13.8m, 2021–2028 [R06] | Overseas placements are not domestic absorption; diaspora investment is selective, and commitments are not verified 2026 jobs delivered. |
| EU-supported mobility, including THAMM | Strengthens legal migration governance, qualification recognition and mobility | ETF September 2021 describes coverage of Tunisia, Morocco and Egypt; Tunisia-specific current beneficiary number not authenticated [R06] | Mobility is useful but generally requires recognised capabilities, language and selection. It may relieve individual unemployment while reducing domestic scarce skills. Earlier HOMERe/MENTOR phases are historical, not assumed active today. |
| World Bank TEEP and STEEIR | Improves tertiary programmes, employer links, institutional quality and digital capabilities | R05 reports TEEP USD70m, 2016–2024, over 400 quality subprojects; STEEIR USD100m implementation plan 2026–2031 [R05] | Student/institution-centred investment does not automatically provide payroll-backed re-entry for older alumni. Project budgets, services/users and curricula are not employment counts. |

An effective older-cohort response would combine authenticated outreach with assessment of prior learning, limited paid refresher learning, lawful contracts, geographic access, reasonable adjustments and work commissioned by identifiable beneficiaries. It would avoid age cut-offs copied from youth indicators, distinguish programme eligibility from employer preferences, and measure sustained paid employment rather than training attendance. W5D's architecture can organise such a response only if it supplies financing and legally competent delivery partners; the CMS cannot substitute for either. [R01; R02; R05–R07; W01]

## Section 3 — The W5D macro-level solution

### A. The structural thesis

The case for W5D starts with a coordination hypothesis, not a proof that markets can never employ these graduates. Historical graduate output exceeded net creation of high-end occupations; current INS estimates still show particularly high graduate and female unemployment. Firms simultaneously report skills difficulties. These findings imply that adding qualifications alone is unlikely to remove all constraints, but they do not establish a precise causal decomposition or a current stock of 130,000 continuously unemployed experts. The administrative claim remains unverified here. [R01–R04; G01]

A new organisational layer would pool fragmented needs into commissioned work, specify acceptance standards, allocate tasks and maintain reliable evidence of delivery. A small municipality, archive or laboratory may need technical support without being able to recruit an entire specialist team. A shared service can reduce those transaction costs. Yet it must identify an authorised purchaser, beneficiary or sponsor and finance execution. Aggregating unpaid needs does not turn them into effective economic demand. [R02; R03; R08]

Training, private-sector reform and appropriate public recruitment remain complementary. W5D is not evidence that they should stop. Its additionality must be tested against displacement: work bought through W5D should not merely substitute subsidised labour for existing employees or duplicate services already supplied effectively. Paid retention, beneficiary acceptance, unit costs and sustained usefulness matter more than the number of accounts created. [R04; R07; W01]

### B. The five macro works as a demand map

Cultures/Humanities names memory, language and meaning; Built Environment names shelter, infrastructure and inhabited space; Sciences names systematic inquiry and reliable measurement; Governance names rules, legitimate decisions and accountability; Technology names deployable technical capabilities. The register partitions those domains into concrete services. It is an ontology because it organises relationships between kinds of need, expertise, evidence and output, not merely a sales menu. [W01; W02]

This is broader than an IT-only demand map. Water quality needs sampling, lawful standards, physical treatment, data systems and public communication. Heritage conservation similarly combines custody, materials knowledge, building safety and digital access. Recent digital-demand research supports hybrid skills across sectors, while climate evidence identifies physical needs that software cannot satisfy alone. These examples justify cross-domain coordination, not the empirical optimality of precisely five categories or equal staffing. [R05; R08]

A sceptical economist should therefore require a commissioning pipeline for each service: problem owner, lawful scope, accepted work package, resources, price and renewal decision. No source verifies that every registered niche can immediately absorb a fully staffed service. Quantum research, specialist laboratories and clinical support especially require scarce infrastructure and competent supervisors. Their capacity ceiling must not become a hiring quota detached from verified work. [W02; R03; R05]

### C. The 1,000-per-service rule

The design equation is 1,000 experts × 26 services × five macro works = 130,000 expert places. Common service caps make workloads comparable, enable standard evidence schemas and compress reporting into service and macro scorecards. A consistent unit also simplifies capacity checks and recruitment staging. This is a load-bearing organisational convention, not a labour-market estimate or a demonstrated production optimum. [W01; W02]

The costs are substantial. One leader cannot personally supervise 100 managers through weekly individual meetings. The README offers an optional cluster-lead flag; this dossier recommends making clustered coordination operationally mandatory at full scale while retaining formal scopes and rotating reviews. The manager cap is 12, with a soft target near ten; service capacity remains 1,000. Clusters cannot create another unaccountable chain of approvals. [W01]

Headcount accounting must be settled. With managers outside the expert cap, the hierarchy contains 130,000 members plus 13,000 managers, 130 leaders and one owner: 143,131 operational accounts before additional administrative/commercial roles. If managers are included within each 1,000, the expert/manager ratio changes toward nine. The README permits that configuration but leaves a decision to settings. Payroll and output denominators must use the chosen configuration consistently; the salary arithmetic below covers members only in the outside-manager baseline. [W01]

### D. Dyon certification as the entry gate

Dyon supplies a potential connection between identity, competency claims, check-ins and submitted work. The README names QR identity, certification status, permissions and continuing modules. It does not publish competency levels, a signed credential format, revocation logic or proof that activation is technically blocked without certification. Consequently, a valid-Dyon-before-production rule is a recommended launch condition, not an already verified control. [W01]

That gate would allow an investor to distinguish an assessed, assigned person from an anonymous headcount, give a leader a documented scope of competence, and attach evidence to an accountable account. Assessment should recognise prior learning and provide accessible retesting and appeal. A QR proves neither professional licensure nor physical presence or output quality by itself; lawful clinical, engineering and legal authorisations remain separate. [W01; R06; R07]

The requested 5% audit is also a proposed enhancement. At full capacity it means 50 reports per service and 6,500 across the workforce each week. The README's leader schedule instead specifies 20 random reports per service: 2% of 1,000. Increasing this workload needs staffing, random-selection records and independent checks. Managers still review every report. Statistical sampling detects some defects; it does not certify all unsampled work or make organised fraud impossible. [W01; design arithmetic]

### E. The weekly work engine as coordination fabric

The engine converts broad commitments into named assignments and accepted outputs. In Africa/Tunis time, the owner reviews the previous week Monday 08:00 and publishes directives at 09:00. Leaders allocate by 11:00, managers assign by 14:00, and experts accept by 17:00. Wednesday blocker escalation reaches leaders by 12:00 and the owner by 16:00. Reports close Friday 12:00, manager decisions by 16:00, leader sign-off and locking by 18:00; final rollups follow Saturday 02:00. [W01]

These deadlines make missing inputs visible before aggregated success is announced. The general escalation ladder is manager handling within 24 hours, leader escalation at 48 hours, then owner review of priority blockers. Immediate escalation for safety, privacy or unlawful-payment problems is proposed rather than delayed until the weekly list. The README's Monday 08:00 leader-reading slot precedes publication; current directives must therefore be read as drafts until 09:00, not silently treated as already final. [W01]

Numerical RAG settings are unspecified in the README. Proposed pilot thresholds are green for at least 95% accepted on-time eligible reports with no unresolved critical blocker, amber from 85% to below 95%, and red below 85% or on a critical safety/privacy/payroll failure. Approved leave and reasonable adjustments require explicit denominator rules. Output quality and seriousness of defects must override a superficially high reporting rate. These thresholds need owner approval and service-specific calibration. [W01; proposed policy]

### F. The investment model

A recurring part costs 10 TND daily or 70 weekly. On the README's 30-day convention it supplies 300 TND monthly; the certified post offers 600 TND monthly salary. Thus one part leaves 300 TND uncovered per member post. At 130,000 member posts, salary alone is 78m TND monthly; one part each brings 39m and leaves 39m. These are design calculations, not collected revenue or payroll already paid. [W01]

| Option requiring owner decision | Monthly salary resources per post, 30-day convention | Salary gap | Full-scale implication |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Two recurring parts | 2 × 10 × 30 = 600 TND | 0 TND | 260,000 recurring parts; 78m TND/month salary resources. |
| One part plus committed co-funder | 300 + 300 = 600 TND | 0 only if co-funding collected | 39m TND/month parts plus 39m TND/month co-funding. |
| Scaled salary offer | 300 TND resources, revised 300 TND salary | 0 against revised offer, not the original | 39m TND/month salary; lawful hours, minimum remuneration and social-insurance obligations must be reviewed. |

The README's phrase “600 TND/part/day” in option one is dimensionally erroneous; two parts produce 20 TND/day, not 600. Nor is every month 30 days: 365 daily payments produce 3,650 TND annually versus 7,200 salary, leaving 3,550; 52 weekly payments produce 3,640, leaving 3,560. Two daily parts produce 7,300 annually, just 100 above salary before other costs. Calendar and collection conventions require contracts. [W01; derived arithmetic]

Management outside the member cap, employer charges, leave coverage, equipment, secure evidence storage and reserves are additional. The owner must select and publish one model in settings before onboarding and demonstrate funded-before-filled capacity. This dossier does not make that commercial choice. Leaving it unresolved is the largest immediate payroll-design risk because every accepted member adds a recurring obligation. The pre-2027 hiring horizon is the requested planning target; the README's licensing promotion and countdown do not prove a financed hiring promise. [W01]

### G. What W5D does not do

Credible operating boundaries would prohibit replacing statutory public authority, awarding academic diplomas through work reporting, or selling the same expert's hours repeatedly to different customers. These are proposed safeguards, not invented quotations from the README. W5D may prepare evidence, designs or referrals, while authorised institutions retain approvals, enforcement, judicial decisions and clinical responsibilities. [W01; W02; R07]

Similarly, Dyon cannot replace an engineering licence, laboratory accreditation, ethics approval or a supplier's warranty. Customer contracts must define responsibility for specialist sign-off. A useful workforce coordinates production without claiming sovereign powers or bypassing regulated professions. Universities, public bodies and existing providers should remain partners where their mandates and expertise are necessary. [W02; R06; R07]

### H. Failure modes and remaining construction

**Continued brain drain:** scoped accounts, transfer records and capacity caps help manage vacancies, but do not retain people. Needed additions include credible pay, progression, lawful portable credentials and succession. Certification can increase external employability; coercive retention is not a solution. [R02; R06; R09; W01]

**Leader-span collapse:** caps, rollups and the cluster flag reduce information overload; they do not verify sufficient supervision. Cluster duties, delegated review authority, reviewer availability and absentee-cover rules need explicit design and pilot evidence. [W01]

**Evidence fraud:** approval chains and the append-only scope-crossing audit log improve traceability. Proposed random 5% checks, protected artifact storage, signed manifests, revocation, independent inspection and conflict controls remain necessary. Append-only application behaviour is not cryptographic tamper resistance or proof against database administrators. [W01]

**Payroll gap:** the finance dashboard exposes funding versus payroll, but cannot create money. Enforceable contracts, collection reconciliation, reserves, employment-law review and a funded-slot lock must precede activation. Do not report promises as cash. [W01; R07]

**SQLite Friday peak:** the specification splits content/users from five macro work databases and uses WAL, busy timeouts, short transactions, indexes and rollup-only dashboards. The 130,000 × 52 = 6.76m annual report rows is a design load, not benchmark evidence. Synthetic peak testing, queue monitoring, recovery drills and backups for every database are still launch requirements; macro sharding leaves concentrated bursts possible. [W01]

**Investor default:** portfolio and payroll views support monitoring, not guaranteed collection. Diversification, reserve sizing, default triggers and a lawful continuity plan must be built and stress-tested. No claim here verifies deployed CMS functionality or field performance: the README is an architectural specification, not an implementation audit. [W01]

## Section 4 — How to read the 130 services

Markdown is used because this is a portable repository dossier with traceable headings, tables and technical slugs. All service IDs, English titles and slugs below are canonical. Descriptions, proposed staffing specialities, regional priorities, competency profiles, deliverable quantities and service relationships are **author-designed commissioning specifications**, not established vacancies, contracts, historical achievements or README facts. [W01; W02]

- **Capacity is not a hiring minimum.** Every weekly table assumes a fully resourced, fully staffed service of 1,000 experts, with 100 managers organising approximately ten experts each in the outside-manager model. Phase staffing against verified work and infrastructure; do not recruit 1,000 rare specialists simply to fill a cap. A typical README week includes learning, peer review and reporting, not solely billable production. [W01]
- **“Registered demand” is a proposed intake match.** No authenticated ANETI cross-tabulation establishes available headcount by service, speciality, age and governorate. Priority age bands reflect the older-cohort hypothesis, pending authentication; they are not automatic exclusion rules. A candidate's prior experience and access needs must be assessed. [G01]
- **Regional selections are proposed commissioning geographies**, not claims that measured demand is highest there. Local host agreements, safe travel and access to equipment are prerequisites.
- **Placement preserves the register.** Cultures and Built Environment are Real 1.0; Sciences and Governance are Between 1.0. Technology's macro is Real 0.5 / Virtual 0.5, while the register calls #105–117 “Virtual core” and #118–130 “Real instantiation”. These labels are not measured fractions of hours. [W02]
- **Dyon profiles and activation requirements are proposals.** The README does not specify competency levels. Each profile therefore names a service competency assessment, not an invented Level 2 credential. Dyon never substitutes for a statutory licence. [W01]
- **All weekly targets and KPI thresholds are pilot assumptions.** They refer to completed, accepted work units; related artifacts can document the same underlying case and must not be added as independent economic benefits. Complex projects produce staged packages, not complete infrastructure every week.
- **Evidence architecture is explicit.** The README defines a text evidence field, check-ins and approvals, not a secure artifact repository. Proposed protected object/file storage holds source artifacts and hashes; work databases hold references and decisions. The content database retains the account and scope-crossing audit trail. Retention, encryption and lawful access require implementation. [W01]
- **Sampling proposal:** managers review every report; an independently selected 5% of reports receives service-appropriate re-performance or source verification, with additional risk-based checks. Site reinspection is used where feasible. This changes the README's leader schedule of 20 sampled reports, not an already verified feature. [W01]
- **SDG alignment is a theory of contribution**, not a measured national impact or entitlement to use official labels. Specific target definitions follow the 2030 Agenda. [R11]
- **Dependencies are versioned handoffs.** “Depends on” means an approved prior-week snapshot, not an unavoidable same-week startup prerequisite. “Feeds” identifies a subsequent-week consumer. Relationships are non-exhaustive; initial commissioning uses independently approved baseline inputs. Section 6 explains the unavoidable graph qualification.

### #001 · Heritage Digitisation

**Slug** · `heritage-digitisation`  
**Macro work** · Cultures/Humanities  
**Placement** · Real 1.0  
**Dyon certification profile** · Proposed: `heritage-digitisation` · service competency assessment; level not specified in the README. [W01]  
**Registered demand, Tunisia** · Design intake, not an authenticated ANETI speciality count: archaeology, heritage documentation, geomatics and conservation; diploma levels licence | maîtrise; priority cohort 30–40; proposed region: Tunis, Kairouan and regional partner institutions, with remote preparation where compatible with Real placement. National graduate exclusion supports assessing candidates, not assuming available specialist headcount. The reported older register profile remains unverified. [R01; R02; G01]

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides 3D scanning, archival metadata, virtual museums.

**Short description (FR).**
Numériser le patrimoine avec sa provenance.

**Short description (AR).**
رقمنة التراث مع توثيق مصدره.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Heritage Digitisation service organises a weekly work package around capture packages, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 250 capture packages; 2500 catalogue records; 250 condition sheets; 50 preservation deposits. End-to-end heritage digitisation — field capture via photogrammetry and structured-light scanning, FAIR-compliant metadata catalogues, and immersive virtual museum experiences with ongoing digital preservation. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that capture scale, colour reference and custodial permission must accompany each model. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

The World Bank's 2022 overview compares 64,540 annual university graduates in academic years 2012/13–2017/18 with 10,675 net additional high-end jobs annually in 2011–2017. That historical mismatch supports a broader commissioning hypothesis; it does not establish current vacancies in this speciality. Custodians and communities may benefit without having a budget or a single contracting organisation, so a paying sponsor and reuse agreement must be identified. For `heritage-digitisation`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of capture packages, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R04; R02]

A service leader sets the capture packages acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks catalogue records before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted capture packages from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around condition sheets. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- The World Bank's 2022 overview compares 64,540 annual university graduates in academic years 2012/13–2017/18 with 10,675 net additional high-end jobs annually in 2011–2017. That historical mismatch supports a broader commissioning hypothesis; it does not establish current vacancies in this speciality. [R04]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into capture packages, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for capture packages; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `heritage-digitisation` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence catalogue records and resource-dependent condition sheets before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted capture packages; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Capture packages, accepted against rubric | capture packages | 250 (proposed) |
| Catalogue records, accepted against rubric | catalogue records | 2,500 (proposed) |
| Condition sheets, accepted against rubric | condition sheets | 250 (proposed) |
| Preservation deposits, accepted against rubric | preservation deposits | 50 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `heritage-digitisation` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + TIFF/3D or material-test source files as applicable, linking the capture packages to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that capture scale, colour reference and custodial permission must accompany each model remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: archaeology, heritage documentation, geomatics and conservation.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 30–40 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Tunis, Kairouan and regional partner institutions, with remote preparation where compatible with Real placement (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; institutional authority, consent and lawful access are checked independently of Dyon. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥2 accepted capture packages** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `materials-science` (#059) [t−1] and `data-protection` (#084) [t−1]. Feeds `heritage-built` (#033) [t+1] with the approved capture packages and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 11 · target 11.4; SDG 4 · target 4.7. In Tunisia, accepted capture packages would contribute through paid specialist work, preservation of cultural heritage and access to cultural learning; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Risks specific to this service.**
- Photogrammetry hides surface damage → require competent safety sign-off, controlled trials and a documented stop-work trigger.
- Missing provenance breaks reuse rights → document permissions and obtain qualified rights review before release.
- Fragile objects damaged during capture → require competent safety sign-off, controlled trials and a documented stop-work trigger.

**Sources cited.**

- [R01] — see Section 7.
- [R02] — see Section 7.
- [R04] — see Section 7.
- [R11] — see Section 7.
- [W01] — see Section 7.
- [W02] — see Section 7.

### #005 · Oral History Programs

**Slug** · `oral-history`  
**Macro work** · Cultures/Humanities

**Registered demand, Tunisia** · Design intake, not an authenticated ANETI speciality count: history, anthropology, sociology and transcription; diploma levels licence | maîtrise; priority cohort 40–50; proposed region: Le Kef, Kasserine and Gafsa community partners. National graduate exclusion supports assessing candidates, not assuming available specialist headcount. The reported older register profile remains unverified. [R01; R02; G01]

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides recording, transcription, ethical archiving.

**Short description (FR).**
Enregistrer et préserver les récits de vie.

**Short description (AR).**
تسجيل روايات الحياة وحفظها.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Oral History Programs service organises a weekly work package around interview hours, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 500 interview hours; 250 reviewed transcripts; 250 consent schedules; 100 restricted archive deposits. End-to-end oral history programs — consent-driven recording sessions, professional transcription and translation, ethical archiving, and public access frameworks that honour narrators' wishes. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that narrators retain documented choices over quotation, withdrawal and embargo. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

The World Bank's 2022 overview compares 64,540 annual university graduates in academic years 2012/13–2017/18 with 10,675 net additional high-end jobs annually in 2011–2017. That historical mismatch supports a broader commissioning hypothesis; it does not establish current vacancies in this speciality. Custodians and communities may benefit without having a budget or a single contracting organisation, so a paying sponsor and reuse agreement must be identified. For `oral-history`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of interview hours, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R04; R02]

A service leader sets the interview hours acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks reviewed transcripts before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted interview hours from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around consent schedules. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- The World Bank's 2022 overview compares 64,540 annual university graduates in academic years 2012/13–2017/18 with 10,675 net additional high-end jobs annually in 2011–2017. That historical mismatch supports a broader commissioning hypothesis; it does not establish current vacancies in this speciality. [R04]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into interview hours, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for interview hours; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `oral-history` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence reviewed transcripts and resource-dependent consent schedules before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted interview hours; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Interview hours, accepted against rubric | interview hours | 500 (proposed) |
| Reviewed transcripts, accepted against rubric | reviewed transcripts | 250 (proposed) |
| Consent schedules, accepted against rubric | consent schedules | 250 (proposed) |
| Restricted archive deposits, accepted against rubric | restricted archive deposits | 100 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `oral-history` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + WAV/MP4 master and time-coded annotations, linking the interview hours to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that narrators retain documented choices over quotation, withdrawal and embargo remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: history, anthropology, sociology and transcription.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 40–50 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Le Kef, Kasserine and Gafsa community partners (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; institutional authority, consent and lawful access are checked independently of Dyon. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥4 accepted interview hours** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `social-methods` (#073) [t−1] and `data-protection` (#084) [t−1]. Feeds `official-stats` (#100) [t+1] with the approved interview hours and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 11 · target 11.4; SDG 4 · target 4.7. In Tunisia, accepted interview hours would contribute through paid specialist work, preservation of cultural heritage and access to cultural learning; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Risks specific to this service.**
- Narrators face retaliation → reconcile source records with the interview hours acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.
- Transcription changes meaning → reconcile source records with the interview hours acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.
- Consent does not cover later reuse → document permissions and obtain qualified rights review before release.

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides long-form digital publishing, ISBN/DOI.

**Short description (FR).**
Éditer des publications numériques pérennes.

**Short description (AR).**
تحرير منشورات رقمية قابلة للحفظ.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Publishing & WebBooks service organises a weekly work package around edited pages, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 10000 edited pages; 200 epub validation reports; 200 rights clearance sheets; 50 publication packages. End-to-end digital publishing — editorial workflows, ISBN/DOI registration, EPUB and WebBook production, and multi-format distribution with print-on-demand integration. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that publication requires editorial approval, accessible navigation and rights clearance. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

The World Bank's 2022 overview compares 64,540 annual university graduates in academic years 2012/13–2017/18 with 10,675 net additional high-end jobs annually in 2011–2017. That historical mismatch supports a broader commissioning hypothesis; it does not establish current vacancies in this speciality. Custodians and communities may benefit without having a budget or a single contracting organisation, so a paying sponsor and reuse agreement must be identified. For `publishing`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of edited pages, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R04; R02]

A service leader sets the edited pages acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks epub validation reports before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted edited pages from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around rights clearance sheets. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- The World Bank's 2022 overview compares 64,540 annual university graduates in academic years 2012/13–2017/18 with 10,675 net additional high-end jobs annually in 2011–2017. That historical mismatch supports a broader commissioning hypothesis; it does not establish current vacancies in this speciality. [R04]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into edited pages, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for edited pages; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `publishing` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence epub validation reports and resource-dependent rights clearance sheets before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted edited pages; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Edited pages, accepted against rubric | edited pages | 10,000 (proposed) |
| EPUB validation reports, accepted against rubric | epub validation reports | 200 (proposed) |
| Rights clearance sheets, accepted against rubric | rights clearance sheets | 200 (proposed) |
| Publication packages, accepted against rubric | publication packages | 50 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `publishing` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + redacted source and consultation records, linking the edited pages to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that publication requires editorial approval, accessible navigation and rights clearance remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: publishing, editing, information science and accessible document production.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 30–40 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Tunis, Kairouan and regional partner institutions, with remote preparation where compatible with Real placement (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; institutional authority, consent and lawful access are checked independently of Dyon. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥80 accepted edited pages** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `data-protection` (#084) [t−1] and `cloud-infra` (#107) [t−1]. Feeds `stem-education` (#076) [t+1] with the approved edited pages and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 11 · target 11.4; SDG 4 · target 4.7. In Tunisia, accepted edited pages would contribute through lawfully paid creative work, cultural preservation and access to learning; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Risks specific to this service.**
- Broken identifiers sever citations → reconcile source records with the edited pages acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.
- Unlicensed illustrations block distribution → document permissions and obtain qualified rights review before release.
- Inaccessible files exclude readers → include affected-user review, publish selection assumptions and retain a grievance route.

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides research, facilitation, publication.

**Short description (FR).**
Soutenir un dialogue documenté et volontaire.

**Short description (AR).**
دعم حوار موثق وطوعي.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Interfaith & Dialogue Studies service organises a weekly work package around comparative source reviews, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 100 comparative source reviews; 100 facilitated sessions; 100 anonymised transcripts; 50 teaching resources. Interfaith and intercultural dialogue — comparative research, facilitated dialogue programs, curriculum development, and scholarly publication on coexistence and pluralism. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that participants choose disclosure limits and facilitators document dissent. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

The World Bank's 2022 overview compares 64,540 annual university graduates in academic years 2012/13–2017/18 with 10,675 net additional high-end jobs annually in 2011–2017. That historical mismatch supports a broader commissioning hypothesis; it does not establish current vacancies in this speciality. Custodians and communities may benefit without having a budget or a single contracting organisation, so a paying sponsor and reuse agreement must be identified. For `interfaith`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of comparative source reviews, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R04; R02]

A service leader sets the comparative source reviews acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks facilitated sessions before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted comparative source reviews from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around anonymised transcripts. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- The World Bank's 2022 overview compares 64,540 annual university graduates in academic years 2012/13–2017/18 with 10,675 net additional high-end jobs annually in 2011–2017. That historical mismatch supports a broader commissioning hypothesis; it does not establish current vacancies in this speciality. [R04]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into comparative source reviews, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for comparative source reviews; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `interfaith` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence facilitated sessions and resource-dependent anonymised transcripts before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted comparative source reviews; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Comparative source reviews, accepted against rubric | comparative source reviews | 100 (proposed) |
| Facilitated sessions, accepted against rubric | facilitated sessions | 100 (proposed) |
| Anonymised transcripts, accepted against rubric | anonymised transcripts | 100 (proposed) |
| Teaching resources, accepted against rubric | teaching resources | 50 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `interfaith` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + redacted source and consultation records, linking the comparative source reviews to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that participants choose disclosure limits and facilitators document dissent remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: religious studies, history, sociology and mediation.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 30–40 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Tunis, Kairouan and regional partner institutions, with remote preparation where compatible with Real placement (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; institutional authority, consent and lawful access are checked independently of Dyon. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥1 accepted comparative source reviews** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `social-methods` (#073) [t−1] and `rule-of-law` (#086) [t−1]. Feeds `education-governance` (#098) [t+1] with the approved comparative source reviews and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 11 · target 11.4; SDG 4 · target 4.7. In Tunisia, accepted comparative source reviews would contribute through paid specialist work, preservation of cultural heritage and access to cultural learning; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Risks specific to this service.**
- Participants exposed by affiliation → minimise access, redact released evidence and test the restricted-access workflow.
- Facilitation privileges dominant groups → include affected-user review, publish selection assumptions and retain a grievance route.
- Consensus claims erase disagreement → require independent source checks, a comparator and explicit uncertainty before acceptance.

### #017 · Library Modernisation

**Macro work** · Cultures/Humanities

**Registered demand, Tunisia** · Design intake, not an authenticated ANETI speciality count: library science, cataloguing and information systems; diploma levels licence | maîtrise; priority cohort 30–40; proposed region: Tunis, Kairouan and regional partner institutions, with remote preparation where compatible with Real placement. National graduate exclusion supports assessing candidates, not assuming available specialist headcount. The reported older register profile remains unverified. [R01; R02; G01]

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides cataloguing, discovery systems, MARC/RDA.

**Short description (FR).**
Moderniser les catalogues et services des bibliothèques.

**Short description (AR).**
تحديث فهارس المكتبات وخدماتها.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Library Modernisation service organises a weekly work package around catalogue records, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 10000 catalogue records; 2000 authority record corrections; 500 discovery tests; 100 librarian support sessions. Library modernisation programs — MARC/RDA cataloguing, next-generation discovery systems, digital repository integration, and staff training on emerging library standards. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that catalogue migration must preserve identifiers and accessible search behaviour. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

The World Bank's 2022 overview compares 64,540 annual university graduates in academic years 2012/13–2017/18 with 10,675 net additional high-end jobs annually in 2011–2017. That historical mismatch supports a broader commissioning hypothesis; it does not establish current vacancies in this speciality. Custodians and communities may benefit without having a budget or a single contracting organisation, so a paying sponsor and reuse agreement must be identified. For `library-modernisation`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of catalogue records, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R04; R02]

A service leader sets the catalogue records acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks authority record corrections before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted catalogue records from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around discovery tests. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- The World Bank's 2022 overview compares 64,540 annual university graduates in academic years 2012/13–2017/18 with 10,675 net additional high-end jobs annually in 2011–2017. That historical mismatch supports a broader commissioning hypothesis; it does not establish current vacancies in this speciality. [R04]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into catalogue records, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for catalogue records; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `library-modernisation` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence authority record corrections and resource-dependent discovery tests before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted catalogue records; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Catalogue records, accepted against rubric | catalogue records | 10,000 (proposed) |
| Authority record corrections, accepted against rubric | authority record corrections | 2,000 (proposed) |
| Discovery tests, accepted against rubric | discovery tests | 500 (proposed) |
| Librarian support sessions, accepted against rubric | librarian support sessions | 100 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `library-modernisation` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + redacted source and consultation records, linking the catalogue records to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that catalogue migration must preserve identifiers and accessible search behaviour remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: library science, cataloguing and information systems.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 30–40 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Tunis, Kairouan and regional partner institutions, with remote preparation where compatible with Real placement (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; institutional authority, consent and lawful access are checked independently of Dyon. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥80 accepted catalogue records** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `education-governance` (#098) [t−1] and `software-eng` (#105) [t−1]. Feeds `stem-education` (#076) [t+1] with the approved catalogue records and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 11 · target 11.4; SDG 4 · target 4.7. In Tunisia, accepted catalogue records would contribute through paid specialist work, preservation of cultural heritage and access to cultural learning; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Risks specific to this service.**
- Migration duplicates bibliographic identities → minimise access, redact released evidence and test the restricted-access workflow.
- Licensing restricts discovery access → document permissions and obtain qualified rights review before release.
- Staff cannot maintain imported systems → test operator handover, maintenance dependencies and an available recovery procedure.
