National graduate exclusion supports assessing candidates, not assuming available specialist headcount. The reported older register profile remains unverified. [R01; R02; G01]

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides recording, rights, pedagogy.

**Short description (FR).**
Archiver les spectacles pour la recherche et la transmission.

**Short description (AR).**
أرشفة العروض للبحث ونقل المعرفة.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Performance & Theatre Archives service organises a weekly work package around recorded performance hours, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 300 recorded performance hours; 200 rights schedules; 500 annotated extracts; 100 teaching packs. Performance archives — video and audio recording of live performance, rights clearing, pedagogical extracts, and public access platforms for drama schools and researchers. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that performers and venues clear recording, teaching and publication uses separately. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

The World Bank's 2022 overview compares 64,540 annual university graduates in academic years 2012/13–2017/18 with 10,675 net additional high-end jobs annually in 2011–2017. That historical mismatch supports a broader commissioning hypothesis; it does not establish current vacancies in this speciality. Custodians and communities may benefit without having a budget or a single contracting organisation, so a paying sponsor and reuse agreement must be identified. For `theatre-archives`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of recorded performance hours, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R04; R02]

A service leader sets the recorded performance hours acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks rights schedules before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted recorded performance hours from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around annotated extracts. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- The World Bank's 2022 overview compares 64,540 annual university graduates in academic years 2012/13–2017/18 with 10,675 net additional high-end jobs annually in 2011–2017. That historical mismatch supports a broader commissioning hypothesis; it does not establish current vacancies in this speciality. [R04]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into recorded performance hours, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for recorded performance hours; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `theatre-archives` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence rights schedules and resource-dependent annotated extracts before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted recorded performance hours; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Recorded performance hours, accepted against rubric | recorded performance hours | 300 (proposed) |
| Rights schedules, accepted against rubric | rights schedules | 200 (proposed) |
| Annotated extracts, accepted against rubric | annotated extracts | 500 (proposed) |
| Teaching packs, accepted against rubric | teaching packs | 100 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `theatre-archives` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + WAV/MP4 master and time-coded annotations, linking the recorded performance hours to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that performers and venues clear recording, teaching and publication uses separately remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: performance studies, theatre, audiovisual archiving and pedagogy.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 30–40 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Tunis, Kairouan and regional partner institutions, with remote preparation where compatible with Real placement (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; institutional authority, consent and lawful access are checked independently of Dyon. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥3 accepted recorded performance hours** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `data-protection` (#084) [t−1] and `cloud-infra` (#107) [t−1]. Feeds `stem-education` (#076) [t+1] with the approved recorded performance hours and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 11 · target 11.4; SDG 4 · target 4.7. In Tunisia, accepted recorded performance hours would contribute through lawfully paid creative work, cultural preservation and access to learning; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Risks specific to this service.**
- Performer consent excludes later streaming → document permissions and obtain qualified rights review before release.
- Recording misses spatial context → reconcile source records with the recorded performance hours acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.
- Pedagogical excerpts misrepresent the work → reconcile source records with the recorded performance hours acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.

### #025 · Heritage Conservation Science

**Slug** · `heritage-conservation`  
**Macro work** · Cultures/Humanities  
**Placement** · Real 1.0  
**Dyon certification profile** · Proposed: `heritage-conservation` · service competency assessment; level not specified in the README. [W01]  
**Registered demand, Tunisia** · Design intake, not an authenticated ANETI speciality count: conservation, analytical chemistry and heritage materials; diploma levels maîtrise | doctorat; priority cohort 40–50; proposed region: Tunis, Kairouan and authorised heritage conservation sites. National graduate exclusion supports assessing candidates, not assuming available specialist headcount. The reported older register profile remains unverified. [R01; R02; G01]

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides materials analysis, climate control, restoration.

**Short description (FR).**
Analyser et stabiliser les matériaux patrimoniaux.

**Short description (AR).**
تحليل مواد التراث وتثبيتها.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Heritage Conservation Science service organises a weekly work package around material assessments, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 300 material assessments; 1000 microclimate logs; 100 treatment plans; 50 conservation trial reports. Scientific conservation of heritage materials — analytical materials science, environmental control engineering, restoration planning, and monitoring protocols for preventive conservation. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that sampling is minimally destructive and treatments need qualified conservation approval. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

The November 2023 CCDR documents Tunisia's water, coastal and energy-transition constraints, including SONEDE distribution losses of 34% in 2021. This establishes a need for measured technical intervention, not a funded order for this particular service. Separate asset owners, infrastructure budgets and environmental responsibilities can leave technically useful work uncommissioned. For `heritage-conservation`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of material assessments, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R08; R02]

A service leader sets the material assessments acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks microclimate logs before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted material assessments from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around treatment plans. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- The November 2023 CCDR documents Tunisia's water, coastal and energy-transition constraints, including SONEDE distribution losses of 34% in 2021. This establishes a need for measured technical intervention, not a funded order for this particular service. [R08]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into material assessments, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for material assessments; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `heritage-conservation` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence microclimate logs and resource-dependent treatment plans before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted material assessments; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Material assessments, accepted against rubric | material assessments | 300 (proposed) |
| Microclimate logs, accepted against rubric | microclimate logs | 1,000 (proposed) |
| Treatment plans, accepted against rubric | treatment plans | 100 (proposed) |
| Conservation trial reports, accepted against rubric | conservation trial reports | 50 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `heritage-conservation` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + TIFF/3D or material-test source files as applicable, linking the material assessments to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that sampling is minimally destructive and treatments need qualified conservation approval remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: conservation, analytical chemistry and heritage materials.
- Diploma level: maîtrise | doctorat; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 40–50 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Tunis, Kairouan and authorised heritage conservation sites (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; any regulated task additionally requires the relevant statutory licence, institutional approval or competent authorised sign-off. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥3 accepted material assessments** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `materials-science` (#059) [t−1] and `metrology` (#064) [t−1]. Feeds `heritage-built` (#033) [t+1] with the approved material assessments and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 11 · target 11.4; SDG 4 · target 4.7. In Tunisia, accepted material assessments would contribute through paid specialist work, preservation of cultural heritage and access to cultural learning; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Risks specific to this service.**
- Destructive sampling consumes rare material → reconcile source records with the material assessments acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.
- Treatment reactions accelerate decay → reconcile source records with the material assessments acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.
- Uncalibrated sensors conceal deterioration → re-perform critical checks against traceable references and quarantine invalid results.

National graduate exclusion supports assessing candidates, not assuming available specialist headcount. The reported older register profile remains unverified. [R01; R02; G01]

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides roads, water, drainage, structural audits.

**Short description (FR).**
Diagnostiquer et programmer la réhabilitation des réseaux.

**Short description (AR).**
تشخيص تأهيل الشبكات وبرمجته.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Infrastructure Rehabilitation service organises a weekly work package around asset inspections, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 1000 asset inspections; 500 defect dossiers; 100 rehabilitation work packs; 50 budget sequencing plans. Rehabilitation of critical infrastructure — structural audits, road and bridge renewal, water and drainage networks, and staged rehabilitation programs aligned with municipal budgets. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that inspection severity determines authorised repair priorities and safe access. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

OECD's April 2022 Tunisia survey identifies coastal concentration, housing costs and transport barriers as constraints on matching skilled people to work. The November 2023 CCDR also identifies investment-dependent infrastructure needs; neither finding counts commissioned posts for this service. Project preparation crosses asset ownership, local access and procurement boundaries, so technically viable work can remain fragmented until a lawful client commissions it. For `infrastructure-rehab`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of asset inspections, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R02; R02]

A service leader sets the asset inspections acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks defect dossiers before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted asset inspections from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around rehabilitation work packs. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- OECD's April 2022 Tunisia survey identifies coastal concentration, housing costs and transport barriers as constraints on matching skilled people to work. The November 2023 CCDR also identifies investment-dependent infrastructure needs; neither finding counts commissioned posts for this service. [R02]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into asset inspections, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for asset inspections; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `infrastructure-rehab` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence defect dossiers and resource-dependent rehabilitation work packs before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted asset inspections; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Asset inspections, accepted against rubric | asset inspections | 1,000 (proposed) |
| Defect dossiers, accepted against rubric | defect dossiers | 500 (proposed) |
| Rehabilitation work packs, accepted against rubric | rehabilitation work packs | 100 (proposed) |
| Budget sequencing plans, accepted against rubric | budget sequencing plans | 50 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `infrastructure-rehab` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + georeferenced inspection/photo or design files, linking the asset inspections to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that inspection severity determines authorised repair priorities and safe access remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: civil engineering, architecture, urban planning, surveying and building services.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise | ingénieur; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 30–40 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Kasserine, Kairouan, Gafsa and authorised coastal project sites, conditional on local commissioning (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; any regulated task additionally requires the relevant statutory licence, institutional approval or competent authorised sign-off. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥8 accepted asset inspections** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `materials-science` (#059) [t−1] and `utility-regulation` (#099) [t−1]. Feeds `energy-audits` (#124) [t+1] with the approved asset inspections and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 11 · target 11.3; SDG 9 · target 9.1. In Tunisia, accepted asset inspections would contribute through paid technical work and more reliable, inclusive infrastructure planning; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

- Hidden defects escape visual inspection → reconcile source records with the asset inspections acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.
- Repairs transfer flooding downstream → test operator handover, maintenance dependencies and an available recovery procedure.
- Poor sequencing interrupts essential services → reconcile source records with the asset inspections acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.

### #033 · Heritage Built Environment

**Slug** · `heritage-built`  
**Macro work** · Built Environment  
**Placement** · Real 1.0  
**Dyon certification profile** · Proposed: `heritage-built` · service competency assessment; level not specified in the README. [W01]  
**Registered demand, Tunisia** · Design intake, not an authenticated ANETI speciality count: civil engineering, architecture, urban planning, surveying and building services; diploma levels licence | maîtrise | ingénieur; priority cohort 30–40; proposed region: Kasserine, Kairouan, Gafsa and authorised coastal project sites, conditional on local commissioning. National graduate exclusion supports assessing candidates, not assuming available specialist headcount. The reported older register profile remains unverified. [R01; R02; G01]

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides adaptive reuse, conservation engineering.

**Short description (FR).**
Adapter les bâtiments historiques sans les dénaturer.

**Short description (AR).**
تكييف المباني التاريخية دون تشويهها.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Heritage Built Environment service organises a weekly work package around condition surveys, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 300 condition surveys; 100 adaptive reuse options; 200 conservation details; 100 heritage impact notes. Conservation-led built environment work — adaptive reuse of historic structures, structural conservation engineering, and heritage impact assessment for new works. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that structural interventions respect conservation consent and existing fabric. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

OECD's April 2022 Tunisia survey identifies coastal concentration, housing costs and transport barriers as constraints on matching skilled people to work. The November 2023 CCDR also identifies investment-dependent infrastructure needs; neither finding counts commissioned posts for this service. Project preparation crosses asset ownership, local access and procurement boundaries, so technically viable work can remain fragmented until a lawful client commissions it. For `heritage-built`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of condition surveys, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R02; R02]

A service leader sets the condition surveys acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks adaptive reuse options before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted condition surveys from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around conservation details. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- OECD's April 2022 Tunisia survey identifies coastal concentration, housing costs and transport barriers as constraints on matching skilled people to work. The November 2023 CCDR also identifies investment-dependent infrastructure needs; neither finding counts commissioned posts for this service. [R02]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into condition surveys, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for condition surveys; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `heritage-built` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence adaptive reuse options and resource-dependent conservation details before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted condition surveys; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Condition surveys, accepted against rubric | condition surveys | 300 (proposed) |
| Adaptive reuse options, accepted against rubric | adaptive reuse options | 100 (proposed) |
| Conservation details, accepted against rubric | conservation details | 200 (proposed) |
| Heritage impact notes, accepted against rubric | heritage impact notes | 100 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `heritage-built` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + TIFF/3D or material-test source files as applicable, linking the condition surveys to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that structural interventions respect conservation consent and existing fabric remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: civil engineering, architecture, urban planning, surveying and building services.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise | ingénieur; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 30–40 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Kasserine, Kairouan, Gafsa and authorised coastal project sites, conditional on local commissioning (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; any regulated task additionally requires the relevant statutory licence, institutional approval or competent authorised sign-off. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥3 accepted condition surveys** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `heritage-digitisation` (#001) [t−1] and `heritage-conservation` (#025) [t−1]. Feeds `eia` (#078) [t+1] with the approved condition surveys and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 11 · target 11.3; SDG 9 · target 9.1. In Tunisia, accepted condition surveys would contribute through paid technical work and more reliable, inclusive infrastructure planning; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Risks specific to this service.**
- Modern strengthening damages historic fabric → require competent safety sign-off, controlled trials and a documented stop-work trigger.
- New use excludes local occupants → include affected-user review, publish selection assumptions and retain a grievance route.
- Missing surveys conceal structural risk → reconcile source records with the condition surveys acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides transit-oriented design, cycling networks.

**Short description (FR).**
Planifier des déplacements accessibles et sûrs.

**Short description (AR).**
تخطيط تنقل ميسر وآمن.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Transport & Mobility Planning service organises a weekly work package around travel survey records, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 10000 travel survey records; 500 route accessibility audits; 100 demand model scenarios; 100 mobility option briefs. Integrated mobility planning — transit-oriented development, cycling and pedestrian networks, demand modelling, and public transport operating frameworks. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that models separate observed travel from assumptions about suppressed demand. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

OECD's April 2022 Tunisia survey identifies coastal concentration, housing costs and transport barriers as constraints on matching skilled people to work. The November 2023 CCDR also identifies investment-dependent infrastructure needs; neither finding counts commissioned posts for this service. Project preparation crosses asset ownership, local access and procurement boundaries, so technically viable work can remain fragmented until a lawful client commissions it. For `mobility-planning`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of travel survey records, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R02; R02]

A service leader sets the travel survey records acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks route accessibility audits before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted travel survey records from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around demand model scenarios. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- OECD's April 2022 Tunisia survey identifies coastal concentration, housing costs and transport barriers as constraints on matching skilled people to work. The November 2023 CCDR also identifies investment-dependent infrastructure needs; neither finding counts commissioned posts for this service. [R02]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into travel survey records, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for travel survey records; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `mobility-planning` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence route accessibility audits and resource-dependent demand model scenarios before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted travel survey records; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Travel survey records, accepted against rubric | travel survey records | 10,000 (proposed) |
| Route accessibility audits, accepted against rubric | route accessibility audits | 500 (proposed) |
| Demand model scenarios, accepted against rubric | demand model scenarios | 100 (proposed) |
| Mobility option briefs, accepted against rubric | mobility option briefs | 100 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `mobility-planning` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + georeferenced inspection/photo or design files, linking the travel survey records to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that models separate observed travel from assumptions about suppressed demand remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: transport engineering, urban planning, geography and survey methods.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise | ingénieur; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 30–40 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Kasserine, Kairouan, Gafsa and authorised coastal project sites, conditional on local commissioning (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; institutional authority, consent and lawful access are checked independently of Dyon. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥80 accepted travel survey records** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

### #041 · Public Space Design

**Slug** · `public-space`  
**Macro work** · Built Environment  
**Placement** · Real 1.0  
**Dyon certification profile** · Proposed: `public-space` · service competency assessment; level not specified in the README. [W01]  
**Registered demand, Tunisia** · Design intake, not an authenticated ANETI speciality count: civil engineering, architecture, urban planning, surveying and building services; diploma levels licence | maîtrise | ingénieur; priority cohort 30–40; proposed region: Kasserine, Kairouan, Gafsa and authorised coastal project sites, conditional on local commissioning. National graduate exclusion supports assessing candidates, not assuming available specialist headcount. The reported older register profile remains unverified. [R01; R02; G01]

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides parks, plazas, accessibility, lighting.

**Short description (FR).**
Concevoir des espaces publics accessibles.

**Short description (AR).**
تصميم فضاءات عامة ميسرة.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Public Space Design service organises a weekly work package around public space audits, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 500 public space audits; 100 co-design sessions; 300 accessible design details; 200 lighting assessments. Public space design — parks, plazas, streetscape renewal, universal accessibility, and safety-focused lighting strategies. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that residents test circulation and maintenance arrangements before design approval. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

OECD's April 2022 Tunisia survey identifies coastal concentration, housing costs and transport barriers as constraints on matching skilled people to work. The November 2023 CCDR also identifies investment-dependent infrastructure needs; neither finding counts commissioned posts for this service. Project preparation crosses asset ownership, local access and procurement boundaries, so technically viable work can remain fragmented until a lawful client commissions it. For `public-space`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of public space audits, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R02; R02]

A service leader sets the public space audits acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks co-design sessions before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted public space audits from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around accessible design details. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- OECD's April 2022 Tunisia survey identifies coastal concentration, housing costs and transport barriers as constraints on matching skilled people to work. The November 2023 CCDR also identifies investment-dependent infrastructure needs; neither finding counts commissioned posts for this service. [R02]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into public space audits, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for public space audits; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `public-space` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence co-design sessions and resource-dependent accessible design details before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted public space audits; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Public space audits, accepted against rubric | public space audits | 500 (proposed) |
| Co-design sessions, accepted against rubric | co-design sessions | 100 (proposed) |
| Accessible design details, accepted against rubric | accessible design details | 300 (proposed) |
| Lighting assessments, accepted against rubric | lighting assessments | 200 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `public-space` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + georeferenced inspection/photo or design files, linking the public space audits to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that residents test circulation and maintenance arrangements before design approval remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: civil engineering, architecture, urban planning, surveying and building services.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise | ingénieur; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 30–40 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Kasserine, Kairouan, Gafsa and authorised coastal project sites, conditional on local commissioning (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; institutional authority, consent and lawful access are checked independently of Dyon. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥4 accepted public space audits** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `social-methods` (#073) [t−1] and `climate-governance` (#090) [t−1]. Feeds `biodiversity` (#067) [t+1] with the approved public space audits and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 11 · target 11.3; SDG 9 · target 9.1. In Tunisia, accepted public space audits would contribute through paid technical work and more reliable, inclusive infrastructure planning; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Risks specific to this service.**
- Beautification displaces informal traders → include affected-user review, publish selection assumptions and retain a grievance route.
- Lighting leaves unsafe blind spots → require competent safety sign-off, controlled trials and a documented stop-work trigger.
- Designs cannot be maintained locally → test operator handover, maintenance dependencies and an available recovery procedure.

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides valuation, feasibility, regulatory mapping.

**Short description (FR).**
Évaluer les marchés immobiliers sans fausse précision.

**Short description (AR).**
تقييم الأسواق العقارية دون دقة زائفة.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Real Estate Market Analysis service organises a weekly work package around transaction verification files, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 1000 transaction verification files; 200 valuation notes; 50 feasibility studies; 100 regulatory constraint maps. Real estate market analysis — valuation, feasibility studies, regulatory mapping, and investment-grade market reports for developers and institutional investors. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that valuations disclose sparse comparables and separate asking from transaction prices. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

OECD's April 2022 Tunisia survey identifies coastal concentration, housing costs and transport barriers as constraints on matching skilled people to work. The November 2023 CCDR also identifies investment-dependent infrastructure needs; neither finding counts commissioned posts for this service. Project preparation crosses asset ownership, local access and procurement boundaries, so technically viable work can remain fragmented until a lawful client commissions it. For `real-estate`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of transaction verification files, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R02; R02]

A service leader sets the transaction verification files acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks valuation notes before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted transaction verification files from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around feasibility studies. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- OECD's April 2022 Tunisia survey identifies coastal concentration, housing costs and transport barriers as constraints on matching skilled people to work. The November 2023 CCDR also identifies investment-dependent infrastructure needs; neither finding counts commissioned posts for this service. [R02]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into transaction verification files, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for transaction verification files; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `real-estate` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence valuation notes and resource-dependent feasibility studies before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted transaction verification files; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Transaction verification files, accepted against rubric | transaction verification files | 1,000 (proposed) |
| Valuation notes, accepted against rubric | valuation notes | 200 (proposed) |
| Feasibility studies, accepted against rubric | feasibility studies | 50 (proposed) |
| Regulatory constraint maps, accepted against rubric | regulatory constraint maps | 100 (proposed) |

A case-linked `real-estate` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + georeferenced inspection/photo or design files, linking the transaction verification files to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that valuations disclose sparse comparables and separate asking from transaction prices remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

National graduate exclusion supports assessing candidates, not assuming available specialist headcount. The reported older register profile remains unverified. [R01; R02; G01]

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides standardised designs, fast delivery.

**Short description (FR).**
Préparer des écoles et cliniques adaptées aux usages.

**Short description (AR).**
إعداد مدارس وعيادات ملائمة للاستعمال.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The School & Clinic Building Programs service organises a weekly work package around facility condition audits, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 500 facility condition audits; 100 standard design adaptations; 300 site supervision reports; 200 accessibility checks. School and clinic building programs — standardised design libraries, fast-track delivery, and quality assurance protocols for ministries of education and health. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that education and health authorities approve layouts and infection-control requirements. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

OECD's April 2022 Tunisia survey identifies coastal concentration, housing costs and transport barriers as constraints on matching skilled people to work. The November 2023 CCDR also identifies investment-dependent infrastructure needs; neither finding counts commissioned posts for this service. Project preparation crosses asset ownership, local access and procurement boundaries, so technically viable work can remain fragmented until a lawful client commissions it. For `school-clinic`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of facility condition audits, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R02; R02]

A service leader sets the facility condition audits acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks standard design adaptations before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted facility condition audits from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around site supervision reports. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- OECD's April 2022 Tunisia survey identifies coastal concentration, housing costs and transport barriers as constraints on matching skilled people to work. The November 2023 CCDR also identifies investment-dependent infrastructure needs; neither finding counts commissioned posts for this service. [R02]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into facility condition audits, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for facility condition audits; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `school-clinic` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence standard design adaptations and resource-dependent site supervision reports before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted facility condition audits; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Facility condition audits, accepted against rubric | facility condition audits | 500 (proposed) |
| Standard design adaptations, accepted against rubric | standard design adaptations | 100 (proposed) |
| Site supervision reports, accepted against rubric | site supervision reports | 300 (proposed) |
| Accessibility checks, accepted against rubric | accessibility checks | 200 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `school-clinic` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + georeferenced inspection/photo or design files, linking the facility condition audits to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that education and health authorities approve layouts and infection-control requirements remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

National graduate exclusion supports assessing candidates, not assuming available specialist headcount. The reported older register profile remains unverified. [R01; R01; G01]

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides protocol design, ethics, site monitoring.

**Short description (FR).**
Coordonner des recherches cliniques autorisées.

**Short description (AR).**
تنسيق بحوث سريرية مرخصة.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Clinical Research Coordination service organises a weekly work package around protocol review packages, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 100 protocol review packages; 100 ethics submission checks; 200 site monitoring reports; 500 training attestations. Clinical research coordination — protocol design, ethics submissions, site monitoring, and Good Clinical Practice compliance for academic and industry sponsors. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that only approved protocols and authorised clinical sites may recruit participants. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

INS/ONM's December 2021 HIMS report estimates that approximately 3,300 medical doctors emigrated during 2015–2020, while INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% in Q2 2026. These different populations show why generic graduate availability cannot substitute for verified health capability. Health research and equipment users need qualified staff, consent, secure information and authorised facilities rather than an unlicensed labour pool. For `clinical-research`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of protocol review packages, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R09; R01]

A service leader sets the protocol review packages acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks ethics submission checks before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted protocol review packages from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around site monitoring reports. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- INS/ONM's December 2021 HIMS report estimates that approximately 3,300 medical doctors emigrated during 2015–2020, while INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% in Q2 2026. These different populations show why generic graduate availability cannot substitute for verified health capability. [R09]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into protocol review packages, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for protocol review packages; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `clinical-research` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence ethics submission checks and resource-dependent site monitoring reports before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted protocol review packages; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

|---|---|---:|

| Ethics submission checks, accepted against rubric | ethics submission checks | 100 (proposed) |
| Site monitoring reports, accepted against rubric | site monitoring reports | 200 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**

The Neuroscience & Cognition Labs service organises a weekly work package around protocol reviews, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 100 protocol reviews; 500 anonymised session records; 500 imaging qc reports; 100 reproducible analysis packs. Neuroscience and cognition labs — experimental design, neuroimaging analysis, behavioural paradigms, and data-management standards for reproducible research. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that participant consent, power calculations and preregistration precede experiments. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

INS/ONM's December 2021 HIMS report estimates that approximately 3,300 medical doctors emigrated during 2015–2020, while INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% in Q2 2026. These different populations show why generic graduate availability cannot substitute for verified health capability. Health research and equipment users need qualified staff, consent, secure information and authorised facilities rather than an unlicensed labour pool. For `neuroscience`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of protocol reviews, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks anonymised session records before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted protocol reviews from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around imaging qc reports. ### #065 · Chemical Safety & Toxicology

**Slug** · `chemical-safety`  
**Macro work** · Sciences

National graduate exclusion supports assessing candidates, not assuming available specialist headcount. The reported older register profile remains unverified. [R01; R01; G01]

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides risk assessment, SDS authoring.

**Short description (FR).**
Réduire les expositions chimiques évitables.

**Short description (AR).**
تقليص التعرضات الكيميائية القابلة للتجنب.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Chemical Safety & Toxicology service organises a weekly work package around chemical inventories, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 1000 chemical inventories; 500 safety data sheet reviews; 200 exposure assessments; 200 control verification visits. Chemical safety and toxicology — risk assessment, SDS authoring, and exposure-reduction programs for labs, factories, and public institutions. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that control recommendations follow actual substances, tasks and authorised exposure standards. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

INS estimates that 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force was unemployed in Q2 2026, while OECD's April 2022 analysis describes weak links between qualifications and employers' practical requirements. Neither statistic establishes the number of experienced specialists available for this scientific task. Laboratory access, supervised methods and continuity of research finance make a collection of individual freelancers an incomplete substitute for an accountable shared service. For `chemical-safety`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of chemical inventories, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R01; R01]

A service leader sets the chemical inventories acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks safety data sheet reviews before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted chemical inventories from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around exposure assessments. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- INS estimates that 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force was unemployed in Q2 2026, while OECD's April 2022 analysis describes weak links between qualifications and employers' practical requirements. Neither statistic establishes the number of experienced specialists available for this scientific task. [R01]
- OECD's April 2022 Tunisia analysis identifies mobility and practical skill-matching barriers; commissioning chemical inventories locally with an accountable reviewer is a proposed response, not a measured employment effect or evidence of 1,000 vacancies. [R02]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for chemical inventories; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `chemical-safety` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence safety data sheet reviews and resource-dependent exposure assessments before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted chemical inventories; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

Food safety and nutrition science — HACCP implementation, labelling compliance, and cohort-based nutritional epidemiology for public health agencies. These different populations show why generic graduate availability cannot substitute for verified health capability. The Social Protection Delivery service organises a weekly work package around eligibility workflow audits, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 300 eligibility workflow audits; 2000 payment reconciliation checks; 1000 grievance file reviews; 200 accessibility test reports. Social protection delivery — beneficiary targeting, payment rails, grievance-redress mechanisms, and interoperability with health and labour systems. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that competent authorities decide benefits and maintain meaningful human review. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

OECD's June 2024 review reports that nearly 40% of covered Tunisian firms identify inadequate workforce skills as a major constraint, using Enterprise Survey comparisons labelled 2020 or latest available. Kotrane's 2024 legal analysis also identifies formal-job scarcity and institutional limits rather than a training-only problem. Benefits depend on legitimate authority, shared administrative records and implementation owners; an advisory product without those users cannot be assumed to improve an institution. For `social-protection`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of eligibility workflow audits, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R03; R03]

A service leader sets the eligibility workflow audits acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks payment reconciliation checks before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted eligibility workflow audits from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around grievance file reviews. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- OECD's June 2024 review reports that nearly 40% of covered Tunisian firms identify inadequate workforce skills as a major constraint, using Enterprise Survey comparisons labelled 2020 or latest available. Kotrane's 2024 legal analysis also identifies formal-job scarcity and institutional limits rather than a training-only problem. [R03]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into eligibility workflow audits, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for eligibility workflow audits; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `social-protection` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence payment reconciliation checks and resource-dependent grievance file reviews before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted eligibility workflow audits; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Eligibility workflow audits, accepted against rubric | eligibility workflow audits | 300 (proposed) |
| Payment reconciliation checks, accepted against rubric | payment reconciliation checks | 2,000 (proposed) |
| Grievance file reviews, accepted against rubric | grievance file reviews | 1,000 (proposed) |
| Accessibility test reports, accepted against rubric | accessibility test reports | 200 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `social-protection` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + redacted source and consultation records, linking the eligibility workflow audits to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that competent authorities decide benefits and maintain meaningful human review remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: social policy, public administration, payment systems and applied statistics.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 30–40 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Tunis and participating interior-region public-service partners; placements follow current legal mandates (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; institutional authority, consent and lawful access are checked independently of Dyon. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥3 accepted eligibility workflow audits** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `rural-settlements` (#043) [t−1] and `software-eng` (#105) [t−1]. Feeds `public-health` (#054) [t+1] with the approved eligibility workflow audits and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 16 · target 16.6; SDG 16 · target 16.7. In Tunisia, accepted eligibility workflow audits would contribute through paid analytical work, accountable institutions and inclusive decision processes; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Risks specific to this service.**
- Registry errors exclude eligible households → include affected-user review, publish selection assumptions and retain a grievance route.
- Payment matching leaks personal data → minimise access, redact released evidence and test the restricted-access workflow.
- Grievances closed without remedy → reconcile source records with the eligibility workflow audits acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.
