National graduate exclusion supports assessing candidates, not assuming available specialist headcount. The reported older register profile remains unverified. [R01; R03; G01]

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides roll management, observation, civic tech.

**Short description (FR).**
Soutenir une participation civique non partisane.

**Short description (AR).**
دعم مشاركة مدنية غير حزبية.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Elections & Civic Participation service organises a weekly work package around accessibility reviews, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 200 accessibility reviews; 200 civic information resources; 100 observation training sessions; 1000 roll quality test cases. Elections and civic participation — voter roll management, election observation, and civic-tech platforms that increase participation. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that only electoral authorities maintain official rolls and accredited observers conduct observation. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

OECD's June 2024 review reports that nearly 40% of covered Tunisian firms identify inadequate workforce skills as a major constraint, using Enterprise Survey comparisons labelled 2020 or latest available. Kotrane's 2024 legal analysis also identifies formal-job scarcity and institutional limits rather than a training-only problem. Benefits depend on legitimate authority, shared administrative records and implementation owners; an advisory product without those users cannot be assumed to improve an institution. For `elections`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of accessibility reviews, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R03; R03]

A service leader sets the accessibility reviews acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks civic information resources before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted accessibility reviews from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around observation training sessions. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- OECD's June 2024 review reports that nearly 40% of covered Tunisian firms identify inadequate workforce skills as a major constraint, using Enterprise Survey comparisons labelled 2020 or latest available. Kotrane's 2024 legal analysis also identifies formal-job scarcity and institutional limits rather than a training-only problem. [R03]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into accessibility reviews, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for accessibility reviews; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `elections` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence civic information resources and resource-dependent observation training sessions before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted accessibility reviews; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Accessibility reviews, accepted against rubric | accessibility reviews | 200 (proposed) |
| Civic information resources, accepted against rubric | civic information resources | 200 (proposed) |
| Observation training sessions, accepted against rubric | observation training sessions | 100 (proposed) |
| Roll quality test cases, accepted against rubric | roll quality test cases | 1,000 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `elections` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + redacted source and consultation records, linking the accessibility reviews to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that only electoral authorities maintain official rolls and accredited observers conduct observation remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: political science, election law, accessibility and civic education.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 30–40 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Tunis and participating interior-region public-service partners; placements follow current legal mandates (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; institutional authority, consent and lawful access are checked independently of Dyon. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥2 accepted accessibility reviews** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `translation-hubs` (#006) [t−1] and `cybersecurity` (#106) [t−1]. Feeds `social-methods` (#073) [t+1] with the approved accessibility reviews and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 16 · target 16.6; SDG 16 · target 16.7. In Tunisia, accepted accessibility reviews would contribute through paid analytical work, accountable institutions and inclusive decision processes; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Risks specific to this service.**
- Partisan selection undermines neutrality → reconcile source records with the accessibility reviews acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.
- Voter information exposes personal data → minimise access, redact released evidence and test the restricted-access workflow.
- Unofficial guidance contradicts electoral rules → reconcile source records with the accessibility reviews acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.

National graduate exclusion supports assessing candidates, not assuming available specialist headcount. The reported older register profile remains unverified. [R01; R03; G01]

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides oversight, complaints, human rights.

**Short description (FR).**
Renforcer les garanties et recours du secteur de sécurité.

**Short description (AR).**
تعزيز الضمانات والتظلم في القطاع الأمني.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Security Sector Governance service organises a weekly work package around oversight procedure reviews, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 100 oversight procedure reviews; 200 complaint pathway assessments; 200 rights compliance checklists; 100 public accountability briefs. Security sector governance — parliamentary oversight, complaints mechanisms, and human rights compliance frameworks for security forces. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that work is civilian governance support, never operational surveillance or policing. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

OECD's June 2024 review reports that nearly 40% of covered Tunisian firms identify inadequate workforce skills as a major constraint, using Enterprise Survey comparisons labelled 2020 or latest available. Kotrane's 2024 legal analysis also identifies formal-job scarcity and institutional limits rather than a training-only problem. Benefits depend on legitimate authority, shared administrative records and implementation owners; an advisory product without those users cannot be assumed to improve an institution. For `security-governance`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of oversight procedure reviews, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R03; R03]

A service leader sets the oversight procedure reviews acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks complaint pathway assessments before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted oversight procedure reviews from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around rights compliance checklists. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- OECD's June 2024 review reports that nearly 40% of covered Tunisian firms identify inadequate workforce skills as a major constraint, using Enterprise Survey comparisons labelled 2020 or latest available. Kotrane's 2024 legal analysis also identifies formal-job scarcity and institutional limits rather than a training-only problem. [R03]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into oversight procedure reviews, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for oversight procedure reviews; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `security-governance` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence complaint pathway assessments and resource-dependent rights compliance checklists before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted oversight procedure reviews; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Oversight procedure reviews, accepted against rubric | oversight procedure reviews | 100 (proposed) |
| Complaint pathway assessments, accepted against rubric | complaint pathway assessments | 200 (proposed) |
| Rights compliance checklists, accepted against rubric | rights compliance checklists | 200 (proposed) |
| Public accountability briefs, accepted against rubric | public accountability briefs | 100 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `security-governance` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + redacted source and consultation records, linking the oversight procedure reviews to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that work is civilian governance support, never operational surveillance or policing remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: public law, human rights, security accountability and complaints administration.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 30–40 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Tunis and participating interior-region public-service partners; placements follow current legal mandates (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; institutional authority, consent and lawful access are checked independently of Dyon. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥1 accepted oversight procedure reviews** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `forensics` (#070) [t−1] and `cybersecurity` (#106) [t−1]. Feeds `social-methods` (#073) [t+1] with the approved oversight procedure reviews and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 16 · target 16.6; SDG 16 · target 16.7. In Tunisia, accepted oversight procedure reviews would contribute through paid analytical work, accountable institutions and inclusive decision processes; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Risks specific to this service.**
- Sensitive complaints expose victims → minimise access, redact released evidence and test the restricted-access workflow.
- Access restrictions conceal misconduct → reconcile source records with the oversight procedure reviews acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.
- Advisory teams exceed lawful oversight mandates → obtain competent legal/authority validation and prohibit unauthorised operational decisions.

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides survey design, dissemination, quality.

**Short description (FR).**
Produire des statistiques avec des méthodes publiées.

**Short description (AR).**
إنتاج إحصاءات بمنهجيات منشورة.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Statistics & Official Data service organises a weekly work package around survey instrument reviews, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 100 survey instrument reviews; 2000 data quality checks; 500 disclosure control tests; 100 statistical release packages. Official statistics — survey design, data dissemination, and quality assurance aligned with the Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that official status belongs to competent institutions, not the W5D service label. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

OECD's June 2024 review reports that nearly 40% of covered Tunisian firms identify inadequate workforce skills as a major constraint, using Enterprise Survey comparisons labelled 2020 or latest available. Kotrane's 2024 legal analysis also identifies formal-job scarcity and institutional limits rather than a training-only problem. Benefits depend on legitimate authority, shared administrative records and implementation owners; an advisory product without those users cannot be assumed to improve an institution. For `official-stats`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of survey instrument reviews, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R03; R03]

A service leader sets the survey instrument reviews acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks data quality checks before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted survey instrument reviews from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around disclosure control tests. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- OECD's June 2024 review reports that nearly 40% of covered Tunisian firms identify inadequate workforce skills as a major constraint, using Enterprise Survey comparisons labelled 2020 or latest available. Kotrane's 2024 legal analysis also identifies formal-job scarcity and institutional limits rather than a training-only problem. [R03]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into survey instrument reviews, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for survey instrument reviews; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `official-stats` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence data quality checks and resource-dependent disclosure control tests before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted survey instrument reviews; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Survey instrument reviews, accepted against rubric | survey instrument reviews | 100 (proposed) |
| Data quality checks, accepted against rubric | data quality checks | 2,000 (proposed) |
| Disclosure control tests, accepted against rubric | disclosure control tests | 500 (proposed) |
| Statistical release packages, accepted against rubric | statistical release packages | 100 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `official-stats` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + redacted source and consultation records, linking the survey instrument reviews to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that official status belongs to competent institutions, not the W5D service label remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: statistics, demography, survey methods and public information.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 40–50 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Tunis and participating interior-region public-service partners; placements follow current legal mandates (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; institutional authority, consent and lawful access are checked independently of Dyon. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥1 accepted survey instrument reviews** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `social-methods` (#073) [t−1] and `data-engineering` (#108) [t−1]. Feeds `digital-humanities` (#007) [t+1] with the approved survey instrument reviews and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 16 · target 16.6; SDG 16 · target 16.7. In Tunisia, accepted survey instrument reviews would contribute through paid analytical work, accountable institutions and inclusive decision processes; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Risks specific to this service.**
- Administrative registries mistaken for representative samples → re-perform critical checks against traceable references and quarantine invalid results.
- Disclosure identifies small groups → reconcile source records with the survey instrument reviews acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.
- Revisions occur without version history → reconcile source records with the survey instrument reviews acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.

### #104 · Treaty & International Cooperation

**Slug** · `treaty-cooperation`  
**Macro work** · Governance  
**Placement** · Between 1.0

**Registered demand, Tunisia** · Design intake, not an authenticated ANETI speciality count: international law, international relations, economics and languages; diploma levels licence | maîtrise; priority cohort 30–40; proposed region: Tunis and participating interior-region public-service partners; placements follow current legal mandates. National graduate exclusion supports assessing candidates, not assuming available specialist headcount. The reported older register profile remains unverified. [R01; R03; G01]

**Short description (EN, ≤ 1 sentence).**
The service provides negotiation support, compliance reporting.

**Short description (FR).**
Soutenir les coopérations et engagements internationaux.

**Short description (AR).**
دعم التعاون والالتزامات الدولية.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Treaty & International Cooperation service organises a weekly work package around treaty obligation matrices, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 100 treaty obligation matrices; 100 negotiation evidence briefs; 200 compliance dossier reviews; 100 partner consultation records. Treaty and international cooperation — negotiation support, compliance reporting, and multilateral engagement frameworks. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that only authorised representatives negotiate, commit or interpret obligations for the state. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

OECD's June 2024 review reports that nearly 40% of covered Tunisian firms identify inadequate workforce skills as a major constraint, using Enterprise Survey comparisons labelled 2020 or latest available. Kotrane's 2024 legal analysis also identifies formal-job scarcity and institutional limits rather than a training-only problem. Benefits depend on legitimate authority, shared administrative records and implementation owners; an advisory product without those users cannot be assumed to improve an institution. For `treaty-cooperation`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of treaty obligation matrices, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R03; R03]

A service leader sets the treaty obligation matrices acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks negotiation evidence briefs before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted treaty obligation matrices from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around compliance dossier reviews. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- OECD's June 2024 review reports that nearly 40% of covered Tunisian firms identify inadequate workforce skills as a major constraint, using Enterprise Survey comparisons labelled 2020 or latest available. Kotrane's 2024 legal analysis also identifies formal-job scarcity and institutional limits rather than a training-only problem. [R03]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into treaty obligation matrices, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for treaty obligation matrices; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `treaty-cooperation` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence negotiation evidence briefs and resource-dependent compliance dossier reviews before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted treaty obligation matrices; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Treaty obligation matrices, accepted against rubric | treaty obligation matrices | 100 (proposed) |
| Negotiation evidence briefs, accepted against rubric | negotiation evidence briefs | 100 (proposed) |
| Compliance dossier reviews, accepted against rubric | compliance dossier reviews | 200 (proposed) |
| Partner consultation records, accepted against rubric | partner consultation records | 100 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `treaty-cooperation` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + redacted source and consultation records, linking the treaty obligation matrices to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that only authorised representatives negotiate, commit or interpret obligations for the state remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: international law, international relations, economics and languages.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 30–40 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: Tunis and participating interior-region public-service partners; placements follow current legal mandates (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; institutional authority, consent and lawful access are checked independently of Dyon. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥1 accepted treaty obligation matrices** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 16 · target 16.6; SDG 16 · target 16.7. In Tunisia, accepted treaty obligation matrices would contribute through paid analytical work, accountable institutions and inclusive decision processes; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Short description (AR).**
تحسين العمليات المنجمية ورقابتها.

**Long description (EN, 120–350 words).**
The Mining & Materials Processing Tech service organises a weekly work package around equipment safety inspections, rather than treating attendance as the product. At full, resourced capacity, its pilot plan is 500 equipment safety inspections; 300 dust control assessments; 100 process balance studies; 300 environmental control checks. Mining and materials processing — extraction equipment, safety systems, and environmental controls aligned with international standards. Specialists sequence those methods against the accepted weekly package. The governing boundary is that mine operators retain safety authority and sampling follows controlled access procedures. These are staged outputs from commissioned cases, not a promise to complete an entire national programme each week.

The November 2023 CCDR documents Tunisia's water, coastal and energy-transition constraints, including SONEDE distribution losses of 34% in 2021. This establishes a need for measured technical intervention, not a funded order for this particular service. Separate asset owners, infrastructure budgets and environmental responsibilities can leave technically useful work uncommissioned. For `mining-tech`, the proposed response is therefore a contracted workflow with a named beneficiary and an accepted definition of equipment safety inspections, not recruitment justified solely by the national unemployment rate. [R08; R03]

A service leader sets the equipment safety inspections acceptance rubric; 100 managers translate it into approximately ten-expert team assignments. Dyon-linked identities identify accountable contributors, while a competent reviewer checks dust control assessments before approval. The proposed 5% random audit rechecks source evidence and exceptions; it does not replace manager review of every weekly report. The service rollup distinguishes accepted equipment safety inspections from rejected or deferred work and records blockers around process balance studies. Cluster-lead reviews coordinate shared resources without increasing the 1,000-expert cap. [W01; W02]

**Problem addressed (Tunisia-specific).**
- The November 2023 CCDR documents Tunisia's water, coastal and energy-transition constraints, including SONEDE distribution losses of 34% in 2021. This establishes a need for measured technical intervention, not a funded order for this particular service. [R08]
- INS estimates graduate unemployment at 26.6% of the Tunisian graduate labour force in Q2 2026; this supports assessed re-entry into equipment safety inspections, not a measured count of specialists or commissioned positions. [R01]

**W5D macro-level solution.**
- **1,000-per-service and capacity cap:** maintain a common staffing denominator for equipment safety inspections; fill places only against approved work and available supervision. [W01]
- **Dyon:** the proposed `mining-tech` assessment and identity-linked acceptance record make competence and responsibility explicit; statutory authority remains separate. [W01]
- **Weekly engine and cluster-lead:** managers sequence dust control assessments and resource-dependent process balance studies before the Friday approval chain, escalating bottlenecks rather than duplicating assignments. [W01]
- **5% sampling and split DB rollup:** proposed random source verification challenges accepted equipment safety inspections; the macro work database aggregates accepted quantities, rework and blockers without dashboard scans of raw reports. [W01]

**Deliverables (what a team of 1,000 experts produces).**
Proposed pilot targets, conditional on contracts, qualified reviewers, lawful site access, equipment and a fully staffed service; not measured output or an employment commitment.

| Deliverable | Unit | Weekly target (per 1,000 experts) |
|---|---|---:|
| Equipment safety inspections, accepted against rubric | equipment safety inspections | 500 (proposed) |
| Dust control assessments, accepted against rubric | dust control assessments | 300 (proposed) |
| Process balance studies, accepted against rubric | process balance studies | 100 (proposed) |
| Environmental control checks, accepted against rubric | environmental control checks | 300 (proposed) |

**Evidence rule (what counts as proof of work).**
A case-linked `mining-tech` acceptance package contains PDF/A acceptance dossier + CSV/JSON source manifest + georeferenced inspection/photo or design files, linking the equipment safety inspections to the source, reviewer, version, exception log and authorisation. **Proposed storage:** encrypted, access-controlled artifact storage with hashes and retention rules; the macro work DB's `evidence` text holds protected references, not public personal records. Dyon QR check-in/out documents authorised Real-placement attendance where applicable; logged outputs support desk work. Managers check every report; **proposed sampling is 5% of service reports each week**, independently selected, with re-performance/source verification and additional risk-based checks. A QR alone is not proof of quality; the rule that mine operators retain safety authority and sampling follows controlled access procedures remains decisive. These artifact/security/sampling details require implementation beyond the README. [W01]

**Expert profile (who is hired).**
- Degree fields: mining engineering, process engineering, occupational hygiene and environmental control.
- Diploma level: licence | maîtrise | ingénieur; assessed competence and experience determine task scope.
- Age cohort priority: 30–40 (proposed re-entry priority, not a verified registry quota or automatic exclusion).
- Region: authorised Gafsa mining and processing sites (proposed delivery geography).
- Dyon prerequisite: proposed service competency assessment, valid identity-linked QR, current task authorisation and accessible re-assessment; any regulated task additionally requires the relevant statutory licence, institutional approval or competent authorised sign-off. [W01; G01]

**Weekly KPI (what "a good week" looks like for one manager's team of ~10).**
Proposed thresholds: **≥9 of 10 eligible weekly reports** submitted by Fri 12:00; **≥4 accepted equipment safety inspections** per team-week, subject to case complexity; **≤1 evidence-related rework request** per team-week. Approved leave/adjustments change the eligible denominator, and critical safety/privacy defects override a green score. These are pilot targets, not established README thresholds. [W01]

**Cross-macro dependencies.**
Depends on `chemical-safety` (#065) [t−1] and `eia` (#078) [t−1]. Feeds `infrastructure-rehab` (#029) [t+1] with the approved equipment safety inspections and acceptance manifest. Each handoff uses an approved version; initial baseline inputs require separate sign-off. These are proposed artifact interfaces, not transfers of statutory powers. [W02]

**SDG alignment.**
SDG 8 · target 8.5; SDG 9 · target 9.5; SDG 9 · target 9.4. In Tunisia, accepted equipment safety inspections would contribute through paid technical work, research capability and resource-efficient modernisation; attribution requires later outcome evaluation and is not established by output counts. [R11]

**Risks specific to this service.**
- Dust exposure underestimated → minimise access, redact released evidence and test the restricted-access workflow.
- Optimisation destabilises waste storage → reconcile source records with the equipment safety inspections acceptance checklist and assign corrective-action ownership.
- Contractor access bypasses mine safety induction → require competent safety sign-off, controlled trials and a documented stop-work trigger.

## Section 6 — Cross-macro dependencies

### 6.1 What is and is not acyclic

Every entry identifies at least two other-macro input providers and a subsequent-week consumer. These are proposed interfaces, not canonical README dependencies. They do not change a service ID, title, macro or slug. They also do not establish procurement authority or a statutory delegation. [W02]

**The literal service-only requirements are incompatible:** a finite directed acyclic graph has a source and a sink, whereas requiring every service to have incoming dependencies and an outgoing feed removes both. The collapsed 130-service relationship graph therefore is **not certified acyclic**; reciprocal operational relationships are permitted and expected.

**Explicit alternative used here:** each node is `(service_slug, ISO_week, artifact_version)`. A dependency supplies an approved prior-week snapshot; an output feeds a subsequent-week consumer. Every directed delivery edge is `provider[t] → consumer[t+1]`, and within an approved version no reverse dependency is created. For any finite commissioning horizon, week index strictly increases along every edge. A directed cycle would require the index to increase and return to its starting value, which is impossible. Thus **the time-unrolled delivery graph is acyclic**, not the unversioned service graph.

Initial inputs at the boundary of the horizon come from approved external/baseline snapshots; a missing prior artifact blocks the assignment or requires an authorised substitute. Versioned artifacts do not make substantive feedback disappear: corrections belong to the following week and must not overwrite earlier signed approvals. Critical safety incidents can stop work immediately without waiting for the next artifact cycle. Within-week task subgraphs require separate sequencing and are not assumed acyclic merely because the cross-service schedule is lagged.

### 6.3 Coordination without double counting

The provider retains responsibility for its accepted artifact; the recipient decides whether it is fit for the receiving task. For example, water/soil assays do not authorise water-treatment release, and a land survey does not adjudicate title. A shared source manifest lets rollups refer to one artifact rather than claim the same work as two independent outputs or twice bill the same expert hours. These controls are proposed interfaces and contractual rules, not features established by the README alone. [W01; W02]

## Section 7 — Source register

**Access date for every URL:** 11 November 2026. Publication date is distinguished from observation date. References are sorted by source/publisher, not by order of first appearance. A range such as [R02–R04] includes each listed identifier. “Proposed” values in Section 5 are dossier design assumptions, not empirical quantities verified by these sources. Institutional reuse of underlying INS/World Bank data is disclosed rather than counted as independent statistical confirmation.

### European Training Foundation

- **[R06]** *Skills and Migration Country Fiche: Tunisia.* **Publication:** September 2021. **Reference:** principally 2019–2021 institutional evidence, with historical migration series. **Population:** migrants, migration institutions, skills systems and programme participants as separately defined; not all unemployed graduates. **Status:** institutional synthesis; ATCT annual 2,000–3,000 placements is a historical reported estimate; EUR13.8m Perspectives is a programme commitment, not a jobs outcome. **URL:** https://www.etf.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-11/etf_skills_and_migration_country_fiche_tunisia_2021_en_1.pdf . Sections on institutions, mobility projects and the way forward support the coordination, recognition and retention discussion.

### Institut National de la Statistique, Tunisia

- **[R01]** *Indicateurs de l'emploi et du chômage, deuxième trimestre 2026.* **Publication:** 15 August 2026. **Reference:** Q2 2026; comparisons with Q1 2026. **Population:** household-survey labour force aged 15+ and separately the graduate labour force; sex-specific denominators apply to sex-specific rates. **Status:** survey estimates, not administrative counts; reported standard errors were not available in the consulted release. Overall unemployed 622,400 and unemployment 14.9%; graduate unemployment 26.6%, women 35.6%, men 14.2%; youth unemployment ages 15–24 is 35.4%, not NEET. **URL:** https://www.ins.tn/publication/indicateurs-de-lemploi-et-du-chomage-deuxieme-trimestre-2026 . The 21.4 percentage-point graduate gender gap is dossier arithmetic.

### Institut National de la Statistique / Observatoire National de la Migration

- **[R09]** *Enquête Nationale sur la Migration Internationale Tunisia-HIMS.* **Publication:** 7 December 2021. **Fieldwork:** July 2020–March 2021. **Reference for specialist departures:** 2015–2020. **Population:** survey-defined Tunisian current emigrants aged 15+, previously resident in Tunisia and residing abroad for at least three months; not the Order's register or every person of Tunisian descent overseas. **Status:** retrospective household-survey estimates. Executive summary, PDF page 12, reports approximately 39,000 engineers and 3,300 medical doctors leaving for work opportunities in 2015–2020. No measured daily flow or 95% IT-engineer share is supplied by that finding. **Publication page:** https://www.ins.tn/en/publication/report-national-survey-international-migration-tunisia-hims . **Full PDF:** https://www.ins.tn/sites/default/files/publication/pdf/Rapport%20de%20l%27enqu%C3%AAte%20nationale%20sur%20la%20migration%20internationale%20Tunisia-HIMS.pdf .

- **[R10]** Niall O'Higgins, *Measuring what matters: NEET vs youth unemployment.* **Publication:** 12 August 2025. **Reference:** methodological discussion and global evidence through 2025. **Population:** young people, normally 15–24 in the article; NEET includes inactive non-searchers. **Status:** dated analytical article, not a Tunisia-specific empirical estimate or press release; the author's disclaimer applies. General rural/urban patterns are not substituted for Tunisia data. **URL:** https://www.ilo.org/resource/article/measuring-what-matters-neet-vs-youth-unemployment .

ATFP institution/speciality counts are descriptive inventory; CIVP/KARAMA descriptions must not be assumed unchanged in 2026. Its approximately 40% skills-constraint passage refers to the Arab region, not a Tunisia-only statistic. **DOI:** https://doi.org/10.4000/12f0v . **URL:** https://journals.openedition.org/rdctss/8655 .

Cited overall 2019 informality of 45% and sector shares use the source's social-security/tax-registration definition. ICT historical formal job growth and regional/skills constraints are not current vacancy counts. **URL:** https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/2022/04/oecd-economic-surveys-tunisia-2022_2e060f8d/full-report/component-5.html . **Book DOI:** https://doi.org/10.1787/7f9459cf-en .

Figure 3.18 reports almost 40% identifying inadequately skilled labour as a major constraint, approximately 44% foreign and 34% domestic; denominators are covered firms by ownership. The sixfold graduates/high-end-job comparison reuses World Bank [R04] and is not independent confirmation. The cited SONEDE loss figures are 25% in 2010 and 34% in 2021; they establish system inefficiency, not a count of procurement-ready posts. **Publication URL:** https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/tunisia/publication/tunisia-country-climate-and-development-report . **Full report:** https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099112723090114652/pdf/P1791300b52c2a0b00b7bd07899c171db5b.pdf .

### Verification conclusion

The document contains all 130 canonical services, with proposed operating specifications rather than assertions of current recruitment. Formal checks cover entry IDs/titles/slugs, required fields, long-description lengths, tables and valid cross-macro slugs. Those checks cannot authenticate unavailable Ministry microdata, prove a market for every capacity ceiling, or verify CMS runtime controls. The requested service-only acyclicity certificate is not supplied because it is incompatible with universal incoming/outgoing relationships; the explicitly versioned delivery graph is acyclic by construction. Primary register verification, approved financial-model selection, lawful pay conditions and funded pilots remain pre-onboarding requirements. No employment or impact guarantee is implied.

# W5D.TECH
